assumptions: countable graph; p>0; fresh independent q-thinning; countably many rational q with pq<p_c(G)
proof_check: Tonelli gives zero conditional survival on a probability-one set for each rational q; intersect countably many such sets and handle countably many components. At p=p_c>0 all hypothetical infinite critical clusters have threshold one.
remaining_gap: Does not show a hypothetical critical cluster actually survives any thinning.

assumptions: injective b-ary tree embedding; b>=2; uniformly bounded ambient corridor length L
proof_check: At depth n there are b^n distinct images inside ambient radius Ln; use n=floor(r/L) to obtain a liminf over all radii.
remaining_gap: Variable-length corridors and repeated vertices are outside this obstruction.

assumptions: bounded degree Delta; positive infimum h over all rooted finite connected sets; independent fresh thinning; (1-q)^h<1/(Delta^2+1)
proof_check: Encode each rooted n-set by a depth-first walk of length 2(n-1), bound its closed boundary by a^n and sum a/(1-Delta^2 a)<1. This is a union bound, not multiplication of conditionally dependent events. Countable rational q and vertices justify the critical-cluster corollary.
remaining_gap: Positive expansion is only a sufficient premise; C003 excludes it on subexponential ambient graphs.

assumptions: spine ray with finite full binary tree of depth n attached at spine vertex n
proof_check: All radii use n=floor((r-1)/2), giving exponential lower growth sqrt(2). Infinite paths need an entire spine tail, impossible at q<1. Distinct sizes of finite deletion components rule out quasi-transitivity.
remaining_gap: Does not refute the quasi-transitive theorem; it refutes transferring growth alone to a random cluster.
